synopsis: ROS appears across the corpus as an integration and simulation tool: NIOSH evaluated CARLA and ROS for reproducing mine environments, with a planned progression from extensive simulation through small-scale to physical testing [f3488]. TERA provides an off-road example, combining Unity and AGX with configurable excavators, environments, ROS integration and terrain-machine interaction [f4129]. ROS recordings are bags containing every message with its timestamp; ROS and Autoware offer bag-replay and simulation examples, but that evidence is explicitly on-road [f13013, f5607]. ROS 2 is identified as the current generation and is integrated in CARLA, Isaac Sim, Gazebo and BeamNG [f16240]. MathWorks lists ROS among its platform interfaces, but ROS-linked components still require medium relative integration effort because materials, actors, dynamics and timing semantics need calibration despite existing transport and schemas [f8383, f8961, f8729].
